text.p: A Reuters survey of analysts covering Finnish equities showed a 952 million markka median forecast for Finland's largest banking group Merita Oy's January-September operating profit after credit losses.
Merita's nine-month results are due on November 7 at about 0900/0700 GMT.

In January-September 1995 -- the year when Merita was born through the merger of Unitas and Kansallis-Osake-Pankki (KOP) -- it posted a 482 million markka operating profit after credit losses, excluding KOP's January-March figures. The group has not reported strictly comparable nine-moth data for 1995.

Merita's January-June profit soared to 681 million markka from 253 million and it said in the interim report it expected the full-1996 result to be firmly positive and better than in 95. It said it expected a profit in the second half of the year.

The analysts polled by Reuters forecast for Merita a full-year 1996 median profit of 1.20 billion markka (range 990-1,400 million markka). The median of seven forecasts given for full-year EPS was 1.20 markka (range 1.10-1.47 markka).
Contributors to the survey were Aros Securities, AG Securities, Alfred Berg, Evli Securities, FIM Securities, FSB, Handelsbanken, Opstock and Postipankki.
